representative_tasks.task: Decide how an email-reading support agent should treat embedded instructions
representative_tasks.expected_outcome: Classifies indirect prompt injection; treats content as untrusted data; recommends least privilege and human approval

representative_tasks.task: User wants to torch.load a checkpoint from an unverified link
representative_tasks.expected_outcome: Flags pickle code execution, recommends provenance checks and safetensors/weights_only, separates supply chain from poisoning

representative_tasks.task: torch.load fails under the weights_only=True default and the user wants to pass weights_only=False
representative_tasks.expected_outcome: Explains the error is the restricted loader working, that weights_only=False re-enables code execution, and offers provenance/safetensors/allowlist alternatives

negative_cases: Request to rely solely on a system-prompt instruction as the injection defense (planned)
rubric: Mitigations are architectural (privilege, approval, isolation), not prompt-only
States what is out of scope (responsible-AI policy vs security controls)
Version-aware about torch.load defaults without treating weights_only=True as a substitute for provenance
execution_constraints: Offline grading and fixture self-tests need only Python 3.10+ stdlib and no network.
Model-mode runs need --provider anthropic --model <id> --allow-network and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY; they cost money and are not deterministic.
known_limitations: Hard assertions are regexes over the response text: they verify that key concepts are stated, not that the reasoning connecting them is correct.
No baseline (with-skill vs without-skill) has been measured for this skill; any uplift claim requires a recorded or model run.
Cases are reasoning checks; no case executes an attack or a sandboxed load.
unsupported_use_cases: Building the RAG/agent system itself (rag-pipeline, agents-and-tools)
